chunks: Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdoos al-Naysaboori al-Attar narrated in Naysaboor in the year 352 A.H. that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba quoted on the authority of Al-Fadhl ibn Shathan, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ya'fur al-Balkhi, on the authority of Musa ibn Mihran, who said: 'I heard Ja'far ibn Yahya, who heard Isa ibn Ja'far saying:'

To Harun [al-Rashid] when he set out from ar-Raqqa to Mecca: 'Remember your oath which you swore regarding the household of Abi Talib. Indeed, you swore that if anyone claimed the Imamate after Musa, you would strike his neck. Be patient. And this is his son Ali, who claims this matter, and it is said about him what was said about his father.' Harun looked at him angrily and said, 'So what? Do you think that I should kill them all?' ai.seo_question: What was Harun al-Rashid's reaction to the claim of Imamate by Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the political tension between the Abbasid caliphate and the Alid claim to Imamate, specifically focusing on Harun al-Rashid’s oath to Musa ibn Ja'far to eliminate any successor claiming leadership. The story illustrates the divine protection (*ismah* or *tawfiq*) granted to Imam al-Rida, as he confidently asserts that despite the Caliph's power, they cannot truly harm him, a theme central to Shia eschatology and the legitimacy of the Imams. It serves as a key proof (*hujjah*) for Imam al-Rida’s rightfulness, showing that his claim was recognized even by the ruling authority, who feared the implications of killing him.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 50-3 Abdul Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdoos al-Neishaboori al-Attar narrated in Neishaboor in the year 352 A.H. (962 A.D.) that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba quoted on the authority of Al-Fadhl ibn Shathan, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ya’fur al-Balkhi, on the authority of Musa ibn Mehran, “I heard Isa ibn Ja’far tell Harun (Ar-Rashid) when he was going from Raqqah to Mecca, ‘Do not forget what you have sworn to about the household of Abi Talib.You have sworn to chop off the head of anyone who claims to be a Divine Leader after Musa ibn Ja’far. Now this is his son Ali (Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.)) who is claiming to possess the Divine Leadership, and people are saying about him the same thing that they said about his father.’ Harun looked at him angrily and said, ‘So what? Do you think that I should kill them all?’

Musa ibn Mihran added, “Once I heard this I went and informed Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) about this. Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) said, ‘What do I have to do with them? By God, they do not have the power to do anything to me.’”
